clue.text: Jack in turn is tribal leader in charge who is chauvinistic

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
taken as written
a go is a turn in a game
taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so take the start of tribal

explanation.surface: A tribal chief who flips allegiances is accused of blind national prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes T, the first letter of 'tribal'; 'who is' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Jingoism is aggressive, boastful patriotism, close kin to chauvinism in its original sense of excessive national pride.

clue.text: Legal expert had project about gentleman on the way up

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: to jut is to project or stick out

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knighted gentleman

explanation.surface: A lawyer once had a scheme involving a man of rank who was rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' reads the gentleman backwards, as this is a down clue, and 'about' wraps the projecting piece round him; 'had' is only a link after the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A jurist is someone learned in law, such as a judge or legal scholar.

clue.text: Household linen used by monkey right inside new York!

indicators.note: inside means these pieces are placed within the others

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for York, as in NY for New York
an ape is a kind of monkey in loose usage

explanation.surface: Tablecloths used by a monkey in New York, an exclamatory tall tale.
explanation.walkthrough: N and Y, the initials of 'new York', go round APE plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: Napery is an old word for table linen, such as tablecloths and napkins used at home.

clue.text: Ancient mariner

parts.note: a cryptic definition: an old seafarer, described in words that recall a figure from the Sinbad stories and Greek sea-god myth

explanation.surface: A reference to Coleridge's poem about an old sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner, but the clue simply wants an elderly seafarer, read as a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means old and a mariner is a seafaring man, so the phrase is an old seaman, also a legendary figure in the Sinbad tales.

clue.text: Motorcyclist's piece of electronic equipment

explanation.surface: A biker carries some electronic kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' and links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrambler rides a motorcycle over rough cross-country courses; it is also a device that encodes speech or signals so eavesdroppers cannot follow them.

clue.text: Current contribution

parts.note: a cryptic definition: what looks like a present-day donation is really the electrical power fed into a circuit, or any contribution put in

explanation.surface: A donation made at the present time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day' but it is electric current, the energy supplied to a device.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is the power or signal fed into a machine, and more generally a contribution of ideas or effort.

clue.text: A quiet corner in church

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quiet
SE, the south-east, is a corner on the compass or of a map

explanation.surface: Somewhere peaceful to sit within a church building.
explanation.walkthrough: SE stands for south-east, read as one corner of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a vaulted recess, usually semicircular, at the east end of a church, a secluded nook beyond the altar.

clue.text: Ancient Jew played harp I understand

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are worked over like notes on an instrument, a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
to see is to understand, as in I see

explanation.surface: Someone says a biblical figure strummed a harp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges only the four letters of the instrument into PHAR; the surface makes it a musician, but the answer is a member of a strict religious sect.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pharisees were a strict Jewish sect in the time of the Second Temple, so one of them is a Jew of antiquity.

clue.text: Some very onerous duties for each person

indicators.note: the run sits within the words of the clue's phrase about duties, with the opening word Some pointing to part of them

explanation.surface: Burdensome tasks shared out among all the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the last letter of 'Some' through 'very' into 'onerous'; 'for' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Each person, taken together, is everybody in the group.

clue.text: Mercy very much liking compassionate act

parts.note: loving is a stronger form of liking
a kindness is a kind or compassionate deed

explanation.surface: Mercy described as fondness plus a sympathetic gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Loving-kindness is tender, merciful benevolence, the biblical word for compassion shown to others.

clue.text: Quick hit I had

parts.note: a rap is a sharp hit or knock
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A fast blow, I confess.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means fast, done at speed.

clue.text: Scamp engineers proving of the will

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
probate is the legal process of proving a will

explanation.surface: A rascal among the engineers interferes in verifying a dead relative's will.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a crossword staple for 'engineers'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled rogue; scamp is a lighter synonym for such a rascal.

clue.text: Jibe at Sam's car crash

indicators.note: a crash smashes the car, so its letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: here the possessive's S is kept as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone mocks Sam after his motoring accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' scrambles SAMS and CAR; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcasm is cutting, mocking language, and a jibe is a taunting remark of that kind.

clue.text: Three in college

explanation.surface: Three people studying at a university college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trinity is the Christian union of Father, Son and Holy Spirit, three in one; Trinity is also a college at Cambridge, Oxford and Dublin.

clue.text: Ben glowering playing on smooth grassy area

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters frolic about and land in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Ben scowls as he plays bowls on a lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges BEN GLOWERING; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowling green is a closely mown, level lawn for the game of bowls.

clue.text: Nudes ate a concoction that made them sick

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters are blended into another order

explanation.surface: Naked diners ate a dish that turned their stomachs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' mixes NUDES ATE A; 'that made them' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling queasy and ready to vomit is what being sick means here.

clue.text: One member permitted what was inferred

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
MP stands for Member of Parliament
licit means lawful or permitted

explanation.surface: A politician is allowed whatever was implied.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is suggested rather than stated, so it must be inferred.

clue.text: In class a pupil relaxed

parts.note: taken as written
a form is a school class
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A schoolchild in class is calm.
explanation.walkthrough: A FORM is a class in a British school, and L marks a learner.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal means casual and unstuffy, relaxed in manner.

clue.text: $1, say

parts.note: a cryptic definition: a dollar given as an example of a basic standard of currency

explanation.surface: A single dollar, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'say' signals an example: a dollar is one instance of the category.
explanation.definitionFit: A currency is divided into standard denominations, and the dollar is the basic one in the United States.

clue.text: Recommend about five different ideas

indicators.note: different means the letters take a changed form, a rearrangement

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Suggest around five alternative notions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges V and IDEAS; 'about' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To advise is to counsel or suggest a course of action.

clue.text: Rises with heated outcome

parts.note: ups are rises, as in ups and downs
hot means heated

explanation.surface: A temperature climbing produces a fiery result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The upshot is the final result or consequence of something.

clue.text: Leo's mum?

parts.note: a cryptic definition: Leo is the Lion of the zodiac, so his mother is a female big cat

explanation.surface: Asking who a boy called Leo's mother is.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo looks like a person's name; it is the Latin for lion and the sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: A female lion is the mother of lion cubs, so a lion's mum is one.

clue.text: Lady had degree from old kingdom

parts.note: she refers to a lady
BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A woman earned her qualification from an ancient realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' and 'from' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheba was the ancient kingdom of the biblical Queen of Sheba, in southern Arabia.

clue.text: How successful mountaineer finished?

parts.note: a cryptic definition: a climber who succeeds finishes high on the summit, and the phrase also means simply finished

explanation.surface: Asking how a triumphant climber completed the ascent.
explanation.walkthrough: The everyday phrase for 'finished' also literally describes a climber who stopped at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Ending up means finally arriving somewhere, and a successful climber's ascent concludes on the peak.

clue.text: Able to enter next time initially

parts.note: to enter a race or contest is to compete

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the words next and time

explanation.surface: Someone capable of signing up for the next event first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes N and T, the first letters of 'next time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Competent means capable and skilled enough to do a job.

clue.text: Lady with blue pencil had head start

parts.note: to blue-pencil is to edit or censor text, from the editor's coloured pencil

indicators.note: the start of the word had is its head, its first letter

explanation.surface: A woman with an editor's pencil got an early advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head start' takes H, the first letter of 'had'; 'with' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith is a woman's first name, and any female name can be clued as a lady.

clue.text: Story going quite a way up

explanation.surface: A tale about something extending high into the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition works through the phrase tall story, an exaggerated tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tale is an unlikely, exaggerated yarn; tall also means of great height.

clue.text: Glowing beer container beside slope

parts.note: a can holds beer
a descent is a downward slope

explanation.surface: A shining can of ale sits beside a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beside' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Candescent means glowing with heat, white-hot.
